title: Holiday Ad Photos and Videos for Gift Season | AIVideosUGC
description: Cover the whole gift season from one product photo: holiday scenes and clips for winter, Valentine's, Mother's and Father's Day without a reshoot.
h1: Holiday Ad Photos and Videos for Every Gift-Giving Season
lead: Each holiday means another decorated set and another shoot you don't have time for. Upload one product photo and get gift-ready scenes for every season, then add the shipping date yourself.
card: Gift-ready scenes for every season, with space for your shipping cutoff or offer.
intro: Holiday shoppers are usually buying for someone else, so they want to picture the product as a gift: wrapped under a tree, opened at the table, or sitting on a loved one's shelf. Plain catalog shots don't give them that picture.

AIVideosUGC puts your existing product photo into seasonal scenes. Make square images for gift guides and product pages, vertical Story and Reels clips with warm light, and fresh versions for the winter holidays, Valentine's Day, Mother's Day or Father's Day from this starting photo. Shipping cutoffs, prices and codes go on afterward in Canva or CapCut, where you can update them as the season moves.

faq.q: Can I turn my everyday product photos into holiday versions?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the photo you already use and describe the scene, such as a wrapped box on a snowy windowsill. Your original stays as it is.

faq.q: How do I add "order by" dates to my holiday ads?
faq.a: Type them in Canva, CapCut or Ads Manager after download. Keeping dates off the generated image means you can change them quickly as cutoffs approach.

faq.q: Can my holiday ad include a famous character or celebrity?
faq.a: Requests involving celebrities, public figures, or characters and logos owned by other brands may be declined. Generic seasonal touches like ornaments, snow and wrapping paper are fine to describe.

faq.q: How should I prepare holiday product photos?
faq.a: Start with a clear product photo, name the holiday setting, and keep the product identity unchanged. Add dates and shipping cutoffs after download.

faq.q: Do I need to decorate a set or book a creator?
faq.a: No. The seasonal scene is generated around the product photo you upload, so no room has to be decorated and no one has to be filmed. Cutoffs and offers are added after download.

faq.q: Can I use the holiday clips and images as paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded files are yours to use in seasonal ads and carry no AIVideosUGC watermark, as long as they meet the platform's current review rules.

overview.h2: Use seasonal detail to explain the gift
overview.d: A holiday scene should answer why this item belongs in the moment: a candle beside a wrapped box, a serving piece on a dinner table, or a scarf laid beside a coat. Choose two or three props that support that use and leave the product's important surfaces visible. The result feels seasonal because of the setting, not because it depends on a generic greeting.

overview.h2: Keep the visual reusable as dates move
overview.d: Make the scene without a shipping cutoff, price, or discount code. AIVideosUGC offers 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4 video shapes and 6, 10, 15, and 30 second lengths, with cost shown before each job. Use 9:16 for a phone-first clip, 1:1 for a gift-guide post, and 16:9 for a wide page when that composition needs it. Add the exact seasonal wording after download so one image can survive a changed deadline.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a real product for a seasonal scene

items.d: Use a source angle that makes the item's size, shape, and finish easy to recognize beside seasonal props.
For a gift box or bundle, name each product and insert that should appear. Check the result against the package before publishing.
Describe a few colors and materials that complement the product; too many competing decorations can hide the item.

results.h2: A seasonal asset set that stays useful

items.d: A square image that shows the product and its gift context clearly enough for a shopper to recognize it.
A short vertical sequence from package to product, with the final frame held clean for your own message.
A lifestyle frame that shows the recipient's setting instead of relying on holiday decoration alone.

scene_recipes.h2: Gift-season scenes with a clear product role

items.d: Three real bottles sit in a shallow gift box with tissue and ribbon, labels facing the camera and no invented lettering.
A candle rests on a winter mantel beside pine branches and soft lights, with the jar and lid fully visible.
A serving board sits on a holiday table beside folded napkins and a bowl, showing the surface and handle clearly.
A hand removes paper from a small box, lifts the product, and pauses on its front detail in a 9:16 clip.

after_download.h2: Add the season's facts after download

items.d: Add order-by dates, delivery notes, and availability yourself so the order-by date can change when the carrier cutoff moves.
Enter prices, codes, and gift-with-purchase terms in an editable layer, then compare them with the current promotion.
Check the product, packaging, and included pieces against what the recipient will receive.
Remove expired holiday language and keep any evergreen product scene that still makes sense for the next gift moment.

visual.overview: Build holiday product photos around one clear gift moment, then add dates or offers once those details are ready.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the only product reference. Preserve its matte graphite over-ear headphones, round leather ear pads, fabric-covered headband and visible metal telescoping sliders. In a warm winter gift setting, an adult lifts this exact pair from cream tissue in a plain kraft box and holds it at chest height. Keep the full headphones visible. Medium close framing with one gentle push-in; end on the headset beside the open box. Warm, soft indoor light. Sound: tissue rustle and soft room tone; no music or added text.
